mainText: This is Dose of Good for Thursday, November 5. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Pancreatic cancer vaccine triggers immune response in 89 of 90 patients. In a phase 2 study in the US, cited from Mayo Clinic, almost every patient evaluated developed an immune response. The result paves the way for further trials. Second: 18-year-old uses AI to detect microplastics in Lake Paranoá. Tom Silva Nunes built an AI-powered device that identifies polystyrene particles in the water, to help monitor pollution in the lake. Third: 11-year-old girl saves school bus driver who couldn't breathe. Bella noticed the driver was struggling to breathe, called her dad and medical help was sent. The school honored her quick thinking. Fourth: Pitanga and cambuci fibers reduce colorectal cancer cells in the lab. Researchers at the University of São Paulo saw cancer cell viability drop in bench tests. There is no clinical use yet. Fifth: Colorado wildlife crossing cuts animal-vehicle crashes by 91%. The wildlife bridge over Interstate 25 has reduced collisions between animals and vehicles since it opened. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
